still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 40.5% ever-used minus 30.1% current = 10.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 46% of current users are on a second or later course (13.8 points). Another 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (13.8 + 3.0) / 40.5 ≈ 41.5% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining ~7.4 points stopped once and have not restarted. That fits one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose weekly and oral weight regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, ~60% on monthly MariTide (clinic or connected home pen), and restart within a year of 36–47%. First-time users added ~3.0 points (~8.3M), mostly through nicotine-cessation fills after the March 2036 approval, the monthly home pen, and the DoD programme. Age check: 0.20×19 + 0.33×30.5 + 0.24×41 + 0.23×27.5 = 3.8 + 10.1 + 9.8 + 6.3 ≈ 30.0. Income thirds average ~29.8, bracketing the national figure. 30.1% of ~276M adults ≈ 83.1M users, up ~6.4M. Payer mix: commercial ~15.0M (18%), Medicare ~14.6M (18%, inside existing codes), Medicaid ~3.8M (incl. ~0.3M tobacco-cessation fills after March 2036), DoD readiness programme ~0.25M, legitimate cash ~32.9M (40%), imported or counterfeit ~16.5M (20%). Sum ≈ 83.05M. The legitimate cash channel breaks down as ~14.6M cash weight, ~9.4M longevity/'metabolic health', ~4.3M calm/focus, ~2.0M Reset compulsion plans (off-label), ~1.4M alcohol, and ~1.2M nicotine cessation. ~18M current users have a BMI under 30 and ~5.8M under 25. Adult obesity is ~31.2%. ~18% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s (12–17s ~2.5%, incl. some off-label teen vaping use; 6–11s ~0.11%). ~53% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~6.6M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~14.6M users, only through the diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. Arithmetic: 14.6M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $37.7B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B; the average net drifted from $225 to $215. The dementia-risk route is ~2.5M × ~$225 × 12 ≈ $6.75B. Part D plans have announced smoking-cessation formulary placement for plan year 2037; no Medicare cessation fills in 2036. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight use. Because federal law requires Medicaid to cover FDA-approved tobacco-cessation drugs, oral semaglutide entered every state's cessation benefit after March 2036, most with prior authorisation and 12–24-week course limits (~0.3M fills by December). DoD Metabolic Readiness Program: ~190k active-duty members on directly observed monthly MariTide × ~$185 federal price × 12 ≈ $422M, plus ~60k recruits on oral semaglutide × ~$110 × 12 ≈ $79M, total ≈ $0.5B/yr from Defense Health Program funds. The TRICARE benefit for dependents and retirees is unchanged.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $3–25 a month across 170+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials sell for $22–65. NMPA approved a domestic monthly GLP-1 Fc-fusion in 2036, with no US filing. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide is CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China supply ~70% of world volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: Amgen cut MariTide cash from $219 to $199 when it launched the home pen (Feb 2035). TrumpRx maintenance is $169 for the Wegovy pill, $139–179 for Foundayo and $209–259 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound. Starting oral doses are still $149. Oral semaglutide for nicotine cessation is $149 a month cash on TrumpRx. Lilly cut retatrutide to $279. Amycretin ($1,249 list) and bimagrumab ($1,150 list) stay mostly on prior-authorised commercial formularies. Employer weight coverage is still 29%, and another ~13% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks (~8.0M enrollees, inside the 15.0M commercial users). Of those enrollees ~6.4M are on MariTide, ~3.1M at clinics and ~3.3M on the connected home pen that logs each dose to the vendor. Total MariTide users are ~9.8M: tracks 6.4M, cash 2.8M, DoD 0.19M, other 0.4M. Route split: orals ~50%, monthly ~12%, weekly ~38%. LSA reimbursement of calm and Reset fees slipped from 19% to 18% of large employers after the Ohio settlement. Gray market: ~16.5M, growth slowed from doubling to +7%. India's B2C export registration (Jan 2035) cut Indian parcel volume by roughly a third. Chinese 'reta' vials through research-peptide storefronts rose to ~5.2M users and filled the gap.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide), clinic-administered and, since Feb 2035, a connected single-dose home autoinjector
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; oral semaglutide for AUD and nicotine cessation)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab; not an incretin)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Aug 2033)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults 18+ (oral semaglutide, approved Mar 2036)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring language; barred by statute for weight indication in eleven states)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Monthly driver, realised through an existing product in a new form: Amgen's sBLA for a connected MariTide home autoinjector was approved Feb 2035. The pen records each dose and transmits it to the prescriber and, with consent, to the employer's wellness vendor. No implant is on the market: the lead osmotic-pump implant entered phase 3 in mid-2036 and has no filing. Nicotine: Novo filed oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation in Feb 2035 on two phase 3 trials (12-month continuous abstinence ~31% vs ~19% placebo, with lower relapse than varenicline in a head-to-head arm), and the FDA approved it Mar 2036. Compulsion: Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 read out positive in Jun 2036 (~35% reduction in PGSI scores vs ~18% placebo). Novo filed in Sep 2036 with priority review, and under the envelope rules there can be no decision before Sep 2037, so compulsion use stays off-label through 2036. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial met its primary endpoint in the CVD population (HR ~0.84). Lilly filed the non-CVD extension Dec 2035, the review was extended after a major amendment, and the decision is expected 2037. No new triple agonist; Chinese molecules are in phase 3 with no US filing. NMPA approved a monthly Chinese GLP-1 in 2036. US net prices still drift down 3–5% a year; brands hold $150–300 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens and markedly lower on low-dose plans. Nicotine-cessation doses (7–14 mg oral) had nausea in ~22% vs ~8% placebo.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; no change in per-user risk.

No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. The first EPI bellwether trial (2035) ended in a defence verdict on causation for the plaintiff's specific case; remaining bellwethers are set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after 2+ years in users 65+, ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Bimagrumab uptake is small (~180k). The DoD programme pairs MariTide with mandatory strength training; early Army data show lean-mass loss at ~25% of weight lost vs ~35–40% in civilian cohorts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code; resistance-training statements on retatrutide and amycretin labels.

safety_ledger.effect: NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy) and optic-nerve injury
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Pooled FDA Sentinel, Nordic registry and VA data (2035) show HR ~2.0 for semaglutide and ~1.6 for tirzepatide, with similar point estimates for retatrutide and MariTide on smaller numbers. Absolute excess is ~0.5–1 per 10,000 person-years overall and higher in users with diabetes, OSA or a crowded optic disc. At ~83M users that implies roughly 3,000–5,000 excess cases a year nationally. Most cases leave permanent partial vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Upgraded from 'very rare' adverse reaction to a class Warnings and Precautions section (Jun 2035): discontinue on sudden vision loss, baseline eye exam advised for prior NAION or crowded disc. The FAA added baseline and annual ophthalmic exams for airmen on any incretin. DoD excludes rated aviators from the readiness programme pending its own eye study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the nicotine-cessation and gambling trial populations.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% in controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The nicotine trials measured SHAPS anhedonia at ~5% vs ~3% placebo at cessation doses, the first randomised low-to-mid-dose data. That is not significant individually but is consistent with a dose relation. Calm, Reset and longevity doses are still unmeasured; the NIH normal-weight cohort has reported baseline only.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. The nicotine label's clinical-studies section reports craving reduction as an efficacy outcome, and that is what makes on-label 'craving' marketing lawful. The FTC–FDA consent orders still bar the four platforms from off-label mood and compulsion claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and among gray users after supply interruptions. Smokers who stop the cessation course regain little weight but relapse to nicotine at rates similar to other cessation drugs after 12 months.
B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; low ferritin in adolescent girls; gray longevity users rarely tested.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years), partial recovery in about half after 12+ months off. The tirzepatide 7-year excess is now nominally significant (HR ~1.3) but small.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide label update under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; decades-long pediatric exposure; repeated cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. ~18M users with BMI under 30. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas still poorly characterised; no new confirmed signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH normal-weight cohort enrolling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~58,000 by mid-2036. No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster. State labs still find 'reta' vials at 0–300% of label and ~18% endotoxin-positive. Poison-centre calls ~7× 2025.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India's B2C export registration in force since Jan 2035; import alerts extended; more states made sale a felony; federal personal-importation enforcement still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR shows partial catch-up in height velocity after puberty onset in some starters; the ~0.7 cm/year prepubertal deficit is not reversed. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA monitoring language retained; eleven state under-12 bans stand; EMA specialist initiation.

safety_ledger.effect: Prolonged adverse effects with long-acting monthly dosing
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: MariTide's long half-life means nausea, vomiting or dehydration after a dose cannot be stopped by skipping the next one. ED visits for persistent vomiting in the 2–3 weeks after a dose rose with home-pen volume, especially among people who self-escalated or combined it with gray oral product.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Home-pen label requires prescriber-led escalation only; Amgen REMS-lite education module; no restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: About 49% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14–16% from 2025, sugary drinks ~13%, and dollar sales flat on price and protein lines. Zip-code planning is standard at Walmart, Kroger and Albertsons. A small counter-niche appeared: 'unmedicated' full-fat, full-portion lines from regional bakeries and dairies in Pennsylvania and Ohio, marketed on the Unmedicated movement's 'Full Plate' mark. It is under 1% of category sales but growing fast in Pittsburgh and Columbus.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~12%; AUD fills keep eroding the heaviest-drinking decile. Nicotine now tells the same story: after the March 2036 cessation approval, Altria and PMI guided US cigarette volume declines to ~10–11% a year from ~8%, and disposable-vape distributors report the first sustained volume drop outside enforcement. Bar closures continue in mid-sized Midwestern cities. Non-alcoholic drinks are near 5% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down and checks smaller; portion tiers are universal. QSR value menus carry lower-income regain markets. In Pittsburgh's Lawrenceville and Polish Hill, a cluster of 'full plate' supper clubs and family-style restaurants trades on visible appetite. On military-adjacent strips near Fort Cavazos and Fort Bragg, the protein-bowl chains that followed the readiness programme compete with barbecue joints.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists still shrinking. Structured athletic wear and resale grow. The Unmedicated movement created a small aesthetic market of soft tailoring, high-waisted cuts and 'body as is' denim from Pittsburgh and Portland labels. Mass retailers set size runs by zip code.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. DoD contracted civilian strength coaches at 40 installations. DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–450. Budget chains bundle a $15 'vision check' with lean-mass add-ons after the NAION warning, which is mostly a marketing move.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage still 29%. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Adherence differentials persist under the 2027 guidance, and the connected home pen makes verification cheaper. Medicaid programmes face mandatory tobacco-cessation coverage of oral semaglutide and are budgeting for it with PA and course limits. Part D premiums rose again for 2036, and plans priced 2037 cessation placement.

pharma.state: Amgen gained most from the home pen and DoD contract. Novo markets the nicotine label directly to consumers, its first on-label 'craving' campaign, and has the gambling filing pending. Lilly holds the top tier with retatrutide and awaits the dementia extension. NAION litigation joined the EPI MDL docket in 2036. Counterfeit-defence and litigation spending exceeds $1.2B a year. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as payment route and motive, and now also as refusal. Lean and scanned means coached. Lean and already thin, on a pill, means the longevity tier. Soft and monthly-bruised means the employer track or, around Army posts, the readiness programme: a uniform body that is lean, high-and-tight and logged. Regained means gray supply interrupted. A new legible body is deliberately soft, eating in public, wearing the Unmedicated 'Full Plate' pin, and it reads as a choice rather than a lapse.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Upper tiers in Austin and Charlotte boast biomarkers and 'never needed it'. Shift leads on the Columbus corridor carry the track body. Gray 'reta' still brings surgical-grade losses and fast regains to Memphis and the Delta. The Unmedicated movement draws most from college-educated under-30s in Pittsburgh, Minneapolis and Portland, from Bread Alone congregations in Appalachia, and from veterans hostile to the DoD programme. Members cross class lines; their unpaid status does not. Its critics point out that choosing not to take a drug is easiest for people who could afford one.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals in high-density zips are short and protein-led. Unmedicated supper clubs revive the long, loud table: second helpings are served on purpose and nobody asks about doses. Bread Alone claims ~950 congregations. Military dining facilities serve 'readiness lines' sized for medicated appetites.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps carry 'biomarker verified' and 'lean-mass verified' tiers. Two now offer an 'Unmedicated verified' badge backed by a $39 dried-blood-spot assay for semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide. 'Reset' badges persist. Mixed couples, one medicated and one unmedicated, are a recognised therapy category.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, craving is noise a subscription manages, and since March 2036 a drug company says so on television, about cigarettes. In lower-income communities appetite still signals lost access and is defended as pride. The Unmedicated movement reframes appetite, desire and even the urge to gamble as evidence of being fully present, 'hungry on purpose'. Unmuted folded into it. The MAHA wing courts it, and fat-acceptance groups cooperate on issues while keeping separate branding.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide, ~5% vs ~3% at nicotine-cessation doses in randomised data. Calm, Reset and longevity exposure (~15.7M licensed plus gray) is still unmeasured. ~8.0M workers are in adherence-verified tracks and ~0.25M service members in a directly observed programme.
interior_life.framing: It is now a product claim. Novo's nicotine campaign ('Quiet the craving') is on-label, and Reset and calm platforms advertise their nicotine-cessation service and let customers apply the word 'craving' to everything else. Employers have retreated to 'wellbeing' after the Ohio settlement. Clinicians still call it a dose-related side effect. The Unmedicated movement calls it 'selling the off switch'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The Southern District of Ohio suit settled in Oct 2035. The call-centre operator removed track enrollment from promotion criteria without admitting liability, and benefits counsel told clients to stop using adherence data in personnel decisions. Overt employer encouragement cooled, but the 30% adherence premium differentials remain lawful, and the connected pen makes them easier to verify. Workers now buy calm and focus themselves, often after seeing the nicotine ads. At Army installations, programme enrollment is voluntary on paper, but failing body composition can block re-enlistment and promotion, and soldiers describe the choice as 'monthly or the tape'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~18% from 2032 in high-density states, and operators lobby the FDA docket on the gambling filing. Vape shops in college towns post 'last flavour' sales. Pittsburgh's 'hungry' music scene (loud, sweaty, deliberately excessive) is the Unmedicated movement's best-known export. Streaming services keep ambient programming for calm subscribers. Stand-ups split into acts about medicated audiences and acts about unmedicated ones.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the leading couples' complaint. Home-pen day replaced clinic day in many households as the monthly ritual. Mixed medicated–unmedicated couples argue over whether one partner's calm is personality or chemistry. Quitting nicotine on a pill raises the same question Reset users faced earlier: changed, or turned down?
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Unmedicated movement has a 'medication status' non-discrimination bill in Congress (no floor vote) and similar bills in five legislatures, none passed. It allied with MAHA legislators and some veterans' groups against the DoD programme, and a House Armed Services amendment requiring an opt-out without career penalty failed 27–31. Gaming money funds opposition to the gambling indication. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Still permissive on products and restrictive at the edges. The FDA approved the MariTide home pen and the nicotine indication, imposed the NAION class warning, and accepted the gambling filing for priority review. The 2034 consent orders and eleven state under-12 bans stand. Telehealth in-person rules for low-BMI adults remain in seven states. Congress passed nothing on coverage.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new federal subsidy. The Medicaid tobacco-cessation mandate pulls oral semaglutide into state benefits by existing law. DoD funds its readiness programme from Defense Health Program accounts (~$0.5B/yr, arithmetic in access.public_coverage), not as a TRICARE benefit change.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Connected-pen dose logs join clinic records, PBM fills, LSA claims and telehealth check-ins in vendor datasets under consent. The Army records programme adherence in the medical readiness system commanders see. Employer use of adherence data in personnel decisions retreated after the Ohio settlement, but premium differentials did not.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program (Sep 2035) offers directly observed monthly MariTide at base clinics to active-duty members failing body-composition standards, with mandatory strength training. The Army recruit oral pilot became policy. Enrollment is ~190k plus ~60k recruits. Rated aviators are excluded pending an eye study after the NAION warning. The FAA requires ophthalmic exams for airmen on incretins. Houston, Phoenix and Jacksonville police departments contract fitness-standard programmes through city health plans, and two big-city fire unions negotiated opt-outs. DOT 2033 guidance for commercial drivers stands.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world volume. India's B2C registration cut Indian parcels without stopping them, and Chinese research-peptide fronts took share. DoD requires US- or EU-finished product for the programme, a supply-chain rule Amgen's Ohio and Puerto Rico plants satisfy. The cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: FDA approves a connected home autoinjector for Amgen's monthly MariTide that logs each dose to prescribers; Amgen cuts the cash price from $219 to $199 and employer tracks begin shifting enrollees off clinic visits
FDA adds optic-nerve injury (NAION) to a class-wide warning for all GLP-1-based drugs after pooled US and Nordic data show roughly doubled risk; FAA orders eye exams for pilots on the drugs

Pentagon launches Metabolic Readiness Program offering directly observed monthly injections to soldiers failing body-composition standards; aviators excluded pending eye study; ~190,000 enrolled by late 2036
FDA approves oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation; Novo's 'Quiet the craving' campaign runs on national TV within weeks and telehealth platforms relaunch around the on-label claim
Novo's phase 3 trial in gambling disorder succeeds; company files for the first compulsion indication in September under priority review, with no decision possible before late 2037
About 40,000 attend the Unmedicated movement's 'Full Plate' gathering in Pittsburgh; organisers report two million registry pledges and unveil a medication-status non-discrimination bill

open_tensions: The gambling filing will decide in 2037 whether 'freedom from compulsion' becomes an on-label claim. If it does, the 2034 consent orders become largely moot, Reset plans become indicated products, and sportsbook and gaming lobbies are already fighting it at the FDA.

The DoD programme makes the drug readiness infrastructure for a quarter of a million service members, while the NAION warning bars aviators and the Unmedicated movement and veterans' groups press for a penalty-free opt-out that Congress has so far refused.

Medicaid is legally required to cover the nicotine indication, and Medicare plans add it for 2037. That is a coverage route opened by a label, not by policy, and states are already testing how far course limits and prior authorisation can hold it.

The connected monthly pen made adherence verifiable at almost no cost in the same year the Ohio settlement told employers not to use it in personnel decisions. The 30% premium guidance still lets them price it.

prose.headline: Quiet the Craving: The Pill Goes On-Label for Cigarettes, the Army Goes Monthly, and the Unmedicated Want Their Hunger Back
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about thirty adults in a hundred take an incretin drug, some eighty-three million people, and two in five have tried one. Growth has slowed, and most of it came through doors already open: cash, the mail, and now a cigarette label. Employers still pay for weight loss at the same 29 percent. Medicare still reaches people only through heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep-apnoea and narrow dementia codes. The list price on the Wegovy box is still $1,349, and the starting pill on TrumpRx is still $149.

The change people notice is the calendar. In February 2035 Amgen won approval for a home pen of its monthly MariTide that reports every dose back to the prescriber, and cut the cash price to $199. Nearly ten million people are on it, and many of them now count the drug in months. Employer wellness vendors like the pen because it makes adherence a data point rather than a promise. The rule letting employers charge up to 30 percent more to the unverified still stands.

In March 2036 the FDA approved oral semaglutide to help adults quit smoking and vaping. For the first time a drug company could say on television what platforms had been forbidden to say since 2034, that the pill quiets craving, as long as it is talking about nicotine. Novo's ads say exactly that. The calm, focus and Reset services that lost their mood claims now advertise their quit-smoking service and let customers draw their own conclusions. Novo's gambling trial succeeded in June, and the filing will be decided in 2037. Until then betting and shopping plans stay off-label, and sportsbooks report less money wagered per account every quarter.

The drugs carry a new warning. In June 2035 regulators moved optic-nerve strokes, NAION, from a very rare footnote to a class warning, after pooled data showed risk roughly doubled. For any one user the risk is still small, but at this scale it adds up to a few thousand partially blinded eyes a year. Pilots now need annual eye exams. The Pentagon's new Metabolic Readiness Program, which since September 2035 has offered soldiers who fail the tape test a monthly injection in front of a nurse, excludes aviators until its own eye study reports. About a quarter of a million service members and recruits are on drug at government expense. Enrollment is voluntary on paper, but soldiers say the choice is monthly or the tape.

The mail still carries a fifth of all users. India's parcel registration took effect in January 2035 and cut Indian packages by about a third. Chinese 'reta' vials sold as research chemicals took up much of the slack. There has been no repeat of the counterfeit insulin pens, but the poison-centre lines are still busy.

Against all this a movement has formed that is defined by what it does not take. The Unmedicated began among young adults in Pittsburgh and on Appalachian church fasting rolls, and has drawn veterans angry about the Army programme. It has supper clubs where seconds are compulsory, soft denim, loud bands, and a dating badge backed by a $39 blood test. Forty thousand people came to its August gathering. Its bill to bar discrimination by medication status has not reached a vote anywhere. Its critics note that declining a drug is easiest for people who could afford one.

Employers have grown quieter. An Ohio call-centre operator settled a lawsuit by promising to stop rewarding monitored enrollees with promotions, and benefits lawyers told everyone else to do the same. The steadiness they used to buy for workers is now sold to workers directly. Couples' therapists still hear about marriages with nothing wrong and nothing happening. Now one partner is sometimes medicated and the other proudly not, and they argue about which of them has changed.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Specialist Marisol Reyes runs the two-mile at Fort Cavazos at 0610 and finishes forty seconds faster than in March. At 0900 she sits in the readiness clinic on the third floor of the medical building. The nurse holds up a card: read the bottom line, left eye, right eye. Marisol reads it. The nurse swabs her belly, presses the pen, logs the dose on a tablet, and says see you the fourteenth.

She keeps her vape in her cargo pocket and doesn't use it until lunch. Then she takes one pull and forgets about it.

In the motor pool, Sergeant Alvarado asks whether she's re-upping. She says probably. He says the tape won't be a problem now. She says no.

At six she drives to Killeen, where Theo works the pit at a barbecue place with a FULL PLATE sticker on the register. He brings her brisket on butcher paper and sits across from her with his own, twice the size. He eats like he's angry at it. She eats four bites and folds the paper over the rest.

The TV over the bar shows a woman on a porch, not smoking, while a voice says quiet the craving. Theo watches it without expression.

"You could get that for the vape," he says. "The Army'd probably pay."

"I'm already on the thing."

"Different thing."

"Same thing."

He wipes his hands. "Do I seem different to you?" she asks. He thinks about it for a long time.
